The goal is not that every cell passes: it is whether the adjusted instruction runs further, completes more and scores higher than before the adjustment.

profile.budgets: The per-task agent and verifier budgets stay exactly as the frozen composition declares them (terminal-bench 900 s, datacurve 5,400 s); nothing is extended, and no condition is relaxed to make a cell scoreable.
profile.maxParallelNote: 3 is the width at which the two previous full runs of this profile recorded zero ECR throttles; the same width is used for both arms so the two runs share one execution profile.
profile.effortNote: max is the only effort this profile declares; the high-effort runs of 2026-10-05 belong to a separate profile delta that is recorded elsewhere and is never merged.

attempts: One frozen headless attempt per task per arm, all 30 corpus tasks, fh_run_full=true (the tracked batches of 10 are drained in corpus order). No cell is retried inside a run, no best-of-N, no evaluator output re-enters an attempt, and the task's own verifier is the only grader.

reMeasurement.why: These four cells are the only corpus tasks already graded for BOTH candidates at this exact profile (control at max: run 37208521326; landing at max: run 37247045143; both re-measured at high effort in runs 37303771385 and 37255314596). A full-corpus run measures every task, so these four are admitted here as declared re-measurements: same candidate, same budgets, same grader, at most one extra attempt each, and never a second chance at that attempt.
reMeasurement.priorVerdictsKept: Every earlier verdict of these cells stays published and is never replaced or reinterpreted; the earlier records stay canonical for their own windows.
reMeasurement.officialMetric: Because four cells carry an extra attempt, the official figure of these two runs is the repaired pass rate over the run's 30 predeclared tasks (scripts/frontier-harness-repaired-reading.mjs --official), with both verdicts of every repaired cell, the class and the extra-attempt count disclosed. The strict passAt1 (exactly one attempt per task) is NOT claimed for these runs and is reported as null.
reMeasurement.otherCells: The remaining 26 tasks carry no prior verdict for either candidate at this profile; their reading is a single first attempt.

predeclaredReading.betterIs: The adjusted arm is read as better than the control arm when it passes strictly more of the 30 predeclared tasks (repaired pass count) — or, failing a strict pass gain, when it keeps the same pass count while completing strictly more cells with a real verdict and no increase in cells without a verdict.
predeclaredReading.completion: Completion is read per arm as: cells with a real graded verdict (passed + failed, i.e. a reward or an f2p/p2p verdict) vs cells left without one (error / not-evaluated / pre-model environment failure / provider transport failure). A cell whose attempt dies without reaching a verdict is a binding failure and is never counted as a loss of capability.
predeclaredReading.score: Score is read per arm as the number of passed cells plus, for the datacurve cells, the recorded partial f2p fraction; pass/fail per cell is never inferred from anything but the task's own verifier record.
predeclaredReading.delivery: Delivery is read per cell on the graded-delivery paths (/app/recovered.json, /app/out.txt): whether the graded path exists at the end of the attempt, and at what time before the budget it was first written. Presence and earlier delivery are the mechanism this study is about (landing the answer before the budget runs out); a cell that still fails after delivering is a delivery with no pass, and is recorded as such.
predeclaredReading.notRequired: Passing every cell is explicitly not required and is never the bar: a loss on one cell does not refute the change, and a win on one cell does not prove it.
predeclaredReading.uncertainty: One attempt per cell per arm; the two arms run concurrently in the same window and share provider load and runner capacity. A cell flip with this design is a diagnostic observation, not an effect size.
predeclaredReading.cost: Every cell whose disposition or failing set regresses against the control arm is recorded as cost even if the reading is met overall.
predeclaredReading.censoring: A cell bounded by its declared budget or a declared stop is a right-censored observation, reported with its span: never excluded, never counted as a gain.

fairnessDisclosures: No user prefix, no task-specific hint, no grader output and no evaluator feedback reaches any arm; the only text delta is the coding Skill instruction (verified above as the only differing config leaf).
One attempt per cell; no best-of-N, no retry-until-pass, no cell exclusion, no latency threshold, no cell dropped for being slow.
Both arms run at the same declared effort, the same width, the same budgets and the same grader, in the same window, so shared provider load and runner contention fall on both arms.
The four overlap cells are disclosed as declared re-measurements above; their earlier verdicts stay published beside the new ones.

Task environments are internet-connected as frozen (the harness makes no closed-book claim), so upstream retrieval is not mechanically excluded: any cell with an upstream-fetch signature is recorded, never credited as a delivery or pass mechanism.
The arm refs are never moved after dispatch; nothing is merged, and this study never publishes pass@1.

Tabulate per arm and cell: disposition, reward, f2p/p2p, terminal cause, call count, duration against the budget, max call span, deliverable presence on the graded paths, first-delivery time, upstream-fetch signature.

Compute per arm the pass count over the 30 predeclared tasks and, because four cells are declared re-measurements, state the repaired pass rate with both verdicts of each repaired cell disclosed (strict passAt1 stays null).
Read the completion and score halves of the predeclaration, then the delivery half cell by cell.
Write the outcome into this file's outcome section, commit and push to codex/prompt-preservation-execution.
Never flip PR #212 on this reading alone: the PR's own gate also requires the F1 contract defect and the review's blockers to be closed.

decision.merge: NOT merged. PR Simon-He95/best-agent#212 stays Draft (head bca0e2e0, MERGEABLE, unchanged by this readout).
decision.failingCondition: The benefit condition: the adjusted instruction did not beat the instruction on main — it lost three passes on the full corpus. The independent review had passed (ACCEPT) and its three renumbering nits were fixed, so of the two conditions only the measured one was available to decide, and it reads against the change.

decision.reviewStanding: The review's ACCEPT remains valid for the text as written (architecture, fairness, hardcoding, pins); it does not claim a benefit, and this readout supplies the benefit measurement the review explicitly left unverified.
decision.whatWouldChangeTheReading: A new predeclared cohort in which the adjusted text passes strictly more of the 30 tasks than main's text — with the same binding discipline, the same window for both arms, and the graded-delivery cells actually delivering — is what would reopen the merge decision. A repeat of this contrast would also be the only way to tell whether the three-cell gap is stable or is run variance, since deliverable existence and pass sets on this corpus have already flipped between windows without any prompt change.
